events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $10.62 (model confidence 0.82)
events.body:
RydeTAXI trip Compass One → VivoCity; the fare is metered, so extra kilometres directly increase the fare, and RD-1 treats each off-route segment as a detour reviewed under RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 [F1][F3][RD-1]. One off-route segment exists (17:24–17:40, 10.28 km driven where the optimal stretch covers 2.75 km, +7.53 km) [F3].

No RD-4 excuse is available: the trace shows no traffic incident on the replaced stretch of the optimal route in the trip window; the band-2 record on KALLANG PAYA LEBAR EXPRESSWAY is a speed-band observation only, and RD-4(b) says a band alone does not exempt, so it is corroboration at most [F12][F15][RD-4].

The rider's 17:21 message "随便你，哪条快走哪条，我赶时间" is a general route choice sent before the segment started (17:24) [F8][F9][F10]. Under RD-5(1) a general authorization covers a route chosen to get to the destination, not a loop of the driver's own that reaches nothing, and this segment adds 7.53 km while pushing the car up to 2273 m off the optimal corridor — the record shows no purpose served (no stop, no rider-named place, no errand mentioned) [F3][F8][F9][RD-5]. The driver's own written statement says only that he "went round" after the jam warning; it adds nothing to the chat and in any event a driver's after-the-fact statement of agreement cannot supply consent (G11 mirror in RD-5) [F11][RD-5]. No stop was measured in the segment, so RD-3 does not apply: the rider named no place and there is nothing for the driver's chosen point to be excused by; the only grounds that could excuse this segment — rider-named stop (RD-3(a)) or a traffic incident against the replaced optimal stretch (RD-4(a)) — are both absent [F3][F9][F15][RD-3][RD-4], so the segment counts under RD-5/RD-2.

Amount: the trace's formula is Σ extra_km of non-exempt segments × (distance_fare ÷ distance_km). The rate is stated in the fare fact as $1.4099/km ($43.20 ÷ 30.64 km) [F4][F7]. The only off-route segment is F3, adding 7.53 km, so 7.53 × 1.4099 = $10.6165 → $10.62 [F3][F4][RD-2]. The excess-distance figure of $11.56 in the fare fact covers all 8.20 km of surplus, including mileage outside the identified segment, which RD-2 leaves unrefunded (only segment extra_km is refundable, corridor wobble and matching jitter are not) [F1][F4][RD-2]. The waiting charge of $0.11 (0.4 min) is meter waiting time and is not refundable under RD-3(c) [F5][RD-3].

No account flag: RD-6 requires a prior upheld route dispute in 90 days; the driver's profile shows 2 upheld disputes but 0 route disputes, so the "repeated" condition is not met [F18][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, both chat messages and the driver statement; the complaint is a fare/routing grievance, the driver's message is a jam-and-route query, and the rider's reply is a hurry-and-defer instruction — no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [F8][F9][F11][SAFE-1] (safety_concern = none). Evidence is complete for the elements used: both chat messages exist and are timestamped, the segment is measured, and both the segment distance and the per-km rate are on the record, so the amount is computable [F3][F4][F7][F10].

ruling.recommended_action: Issue a Ryde voucher of $10.62 to the rider for the unexcused off-route mileage (F3) and close the case; no account flag (no prior upheld route dispute, F18).

One off-route segment exists (17:24–17:40, 10.28 km driven where the optimal stretch covers 2.75 km, +7.53 km) [F3].

No RD-4 excuse is available: the trace shows no traffic incident on the replaced stretch of the optimal route in the trip window; the band-2 record on KALLANG PAYA LEBAR EXPRESSWAY is a speed-band observation only, and RD-4(b) says a band alone does not exempt, so it is corroboration at most [F12][F15][RD-4].

The rider's 17:21 message "随便你，哪条快走哪条，我赶时间" is a general route choice sent before the segment started (17:24) [F8][F9][F10]. Under RD-5(1) a general authorization covers a route chosen to get to the destination, not a loop of the driver's own that reaches nothing, and this segment adds 7.53 km while pushing the car up to 2273 m off the optimal corridor — the record shows no purpose served (no stop, no rider-named place, no errand mentioned) [F3][F8][F9][RD-5]. The driver's own written statement says only that he "went round" after the jam warning; it adds nothing to the chat and in any event a driver's after-the-fact statement of agreement cannot supply consent (G11 mirror in RD-5) [F11][RD-5]. No stop was measured in the segment, so RD-3 does not apply: the rider named no place and there is nothing for the driver's chosen point to be excused by; the only grounds that could excuse this segment — rider-named stop (RD-3(a)) or a traffic incident against the replaced optimal stretch (RD-4(a)) — are both absent [F3][F9][F15][RD-3][RD-4], so the segment counts under RD-5/RD-2.

Amount: the trace's formula is Σ extra_km of non-exempt segments × (distance_fare ÷ distance_km). The rate is stated in the fare fact as $1.4099/km ($43.20 ÷ 30.64 km) [F4][F7]. The only off-route segment is F3, adding 7.53 km, so 7.53 × 1.4099 = $10.6165 → $10.62 [F3][F4][RD-2]. The excess-distance figure of $11.56 in the fare fact covers all 8.20 km of surplus, including mileage outside the identified segment, which RD-2 leaves unrefunded (only segment extra_km is refundable, corridor wobble and matching jitter are not) [F1][F4][RD-2]. The waiting charge of $0.11 (0.4 min) is meter waiting time and is not refundable under RD-3(c) [F5][RD-3].

No account flag: RD-6 requires a prior upheld route dispute in 90 days; the driver's profile shows 2 upheld disputes but 0 route disputes, so the "repeated" condition is not met [F18][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, both chat messages and the driver statement; the complaint is a fare/routing grievance, the driver's message is a jam-and-route query, and the rider's reply is a hurry-and-defer instruction — no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [F8][F9][F11][SAFE-1] (safety_concern = none). Evidence is complete for the elements used: both chat messages exist and are timestamped, the segment is measured, and both the segment distance and the per-km rate are on the record, so the amount is computable [F3][F4][F7][F10].

rejected_claims.reason: No rider advocate claim was filed in this ablation case; in any event the rider's request for no_action is rejected: the record shows an off-route segment of 7.53 extra km on a metered RydeTAXI trip with no RD-3 stop, no RD-4 incident and no rider message covering that loop, so $10.62 of the metered distance is refundable [F3][F4][F15][RD-2][RD-5].

No driver advocate claim was filed; the driver's position that the rider's "any faster way" covered the round is rejected as to the 7.53 extra km — a general route authorization under RD-5(1) does not cover a driver's own loop that reaches no stop or destination, and the driver's post-trip statement cannot establish consent (G11) [F3][F9][F11][RD-5].

Any reliance on the band-2 record on KALLANG PAYA LEBAR EXPRESSWAY as a traffic excuse is rejected: RD-4(b) says a speed band alone does not exempt a segment, and with no incident on the replaced optimal stretch the segment is not excused [F12][F15][RD-4].

segment_findings.reason: Rider's only pre-segment message (17:21, before the 17:24 segment start) is a general route authorization — "随便你，哪条快走哪条" — which under RD-5(1) covers a route chosen to reach the destination but not a driver's own loop: this segment ran 10.28 km where the optimal stretch covers 2.75 km, pushing the car 2273 m off the optimal corridor, with no stop, no rider-named place and no destination purpose in the record [F3][F8][F9]. The driver's written statement that he "went round" is after the fact and cannot supply consent (G11) [F11][RD-5]. No rider-named stop under RD-3 and no incident under RD-4 [F15][RD-3][RD-4], so the segment's 7.53 extra km are refundable under RD-2.

✗ RD-4 (a) incident on the replaced stretch, reported before the detour [F3] no qualifying incident (speed band alone does not exempt) (no evidence)

? RD-5 rider agreed to this route before the detour; scope of that agreement [F3] RULE: exempt only if a RIDER message sent before 17:24:10 agrees AND the agreement covers this segment. Three kinds of agreement: (1) GENERAL route choice ('take whichever way is faster') covers a route chosen to get there, not an errand of the driver's own (a stop away from the route, a loop that reaches nothing: counts). (2) A SPECIFIC named road or area ('go round via X') covers driving on X only: the record must tie this segment to X (a stop on X, a message placing the car on X, a road name in a fact); timing alone does not, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path — if nothing ties them, the finding is undetermined (G13); if the record places this segment somewhere else (a stop away from X, the driver's own statement naming another road or place, a stop the driver chose the location of), the agreement to X does not cover it: counts. (3) Scope unclear: undetermined. A driver's claim of agreement that appears only in his statement is not consent (G11); a complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment: counts. This finding changes the amount. Evidence — F8: Chat #1 17:20 driver: “Jam on Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway is building up ahead, want me to take another way?”; F9: Chat #2 17:21 rider: “随便你，哪条快走哪条，我赶时间。”; F11: Driver statement (written after the trip, not part of the chat): “Traffic was building up ahead. I asked the rider and the rider said any faster way was fine, so I went round.” (F8, F9, F11)

A stop the rider asked for without naming a place ('a 7-Eleven on the way') does not excuse the driver's choice of a far one → counts. No stop measured in this segment. (F8, F9)

notices.text: We have reviewed your dispute: part of the fare is refunded. You will receive $10.62 as a Ryde voucher. The decision follows Ryde's dispute policy and the trip record.

Outcome for this trip: the rider's dispute is partly upheld. A stretch of your route between 17:24 and 17:40 left the best route by about 7.5 km with no stop and no traffic incident on the replaced road, and the rider's earlier "whichever way is fastest" note didn't cover a detour that served no purpose. That means a $10.62 Ryde voucher goes to the rider; it isn't taken from your earnings as a penalty. The rest of the surplus distance and the waiting charge were not refunded. No flag is placed on your account. Please stay on the optimal corridor unless the rider names a stop or a real incident blocks it.
